Screenshot guide

omasnap-git on Omarchy

The main-branch build of Omarchy's native Wayland screenshot + annotation overlay — region capture, OCR, scrolling shots, pins.

Reviewed 2026-11-05 · independent editorial guide

Short answer

Install with omarchy pkg add omasnap-git (about 2 minutes; 1.1 MB download / 2.4 MB installed). It's the bleeding-edge build of omasnap, Omarchy's native Hyprland screenshot and annotation overlay — drag a region, annotate with arrows/text/redaction/OCR, and it's on your clipboard and saved to ~/Pictures/Screenshots. Check the store page's Updated date first: at draft time the -git snapshot (2026-10-08) was actually older than stable omasnap 1.25.0 — default to stable unless you need main-branch commits.

omasnap-git on Omarchy

omasnap-git is the main-branch (bleeding-edge) build of omasnap, a native Wayland screenshot and annotation overlay for Hyprland — drag a region, mark it up with arrows, text, redaction and OCR, and the result is on your clipboard and saved before the preview fades.

TL;DR

omarchy pkg add omasnap-git

Takes ~2 minutes. The store listing reports a 1.1 MB download / 2.4 MB installed. MIT + OFL-1.1 licensed open source, free forever, no paid tier, no account. Version 1.21.0.r81.g6771b19-2 at guide-draft time (store snapshot dated 2026-10-08). Project: omacom/omasnap (572 stars, created Aug 10, 2026).

Getting started (5 minutes)

omasnap-git vs stable omasnap — which one?

This is the honest question, and the answer is not what the name suggests.

  • omasnap (stable) installs a tagged release. The stable package was updated 2026-11-04, and the repo’s latest tagged release is 1.25.0 (Space to hide the recents shelf, fcitx5 IME candidate-window fix, clipboard size limits).
  • omasnap-git builds from the main branch. Its store snapshot is dated 2026-10-08 with version string 1.21.0.r81.g6771b19-2 — 81 commits past the 1.21.0 tag, which predates the 1.22.0–1.25.0 tagged releases. So at draft time, the -git package in the store is actually older than the stable package.

That flips the usual -git logic on its head: normally you install -git to get fixes ahead of the release. Right now you’d install it to get main-branch commits that haven’t been tagged yet — e.g. the open PRs for a [preview] keep option (#209) and keyboard region selection (#210) — but only once the store package is rebuilt from a newer commit. Default advice: install stable omasnap unless you have a specific reason to track main, and check the store page’s “Updated” date before choosing. If the -git snapshot is newer than the stable package’s update date, it’s the fresher build; if it’s older, it’s the staler one. Everything else in this guide applies to both packages — same binary, same keys, same config.

1. The mental model.

omasnap replaces the usual grim + slurp two-step with one overlay: press Print Screen, pick what to capture, and the shot is already copied to the clipboard, saved to ~/Pictures/Screenshots, and floating in a preview you can pin, drag into another app, or open in the editor. The editor is the point — arrows, shapes, highlighter, text, redaction, OCR, scrolling capture — and annotations stay as editable vector layers with full undo history, even if the app crashes (working documents live under /run/user/<UID>/omasnap/).

2. Install and bind a key.

Install, then add the keybindings — the README’s installer does not modify your Hyprland config, so confirm whether the packaged install wires these up for you (see checklist).

omarchy pkg add omasnap-git   # install
omasnap --version             # confirm what you got
omasnap --help                # all CLI modes

Paste this into a Hyprland Lua config loaded after require("default.hypr.omarchy"):

hl.unbind("PRINT")
hl.unbind("F12")
hl.unbind("ALT + SHIFT + 4")
o.bind("PRINT", "Screenshot", "omasnap")
o.bind("F12", "Screenshot", "omasnap")
o.bind("ALT + SHIFT + 4", "Screenshot", "omasnap")
hl.layer_rule({
  match = { namespace = "^omasnap$" },
  no_anim = true,
  animation = "none",
})

Then hyprctl reload and hyprctl configerrors. Each key toggles: first press opens the overlay, next press dismisses it. Do not add no_screen_share = true to the omasnap layer rule — Hyprland replaces an excluded layer’s rectangle with black in captures, which breaks scrolling capture.

3. Take your first screenshot.

Press Print Screen. The overlay opens on the focused monitor:

  • Drag for a freeform region — a pointer-side readout shows the size in native export pixels while you drag.
  • Click a window to capture just that window (a crop of the monitor frame — overlapping windows stay visible).
  • Click open monitor space for the full focused monitor.
  • Press Tab mid-drag to cycle the region shape: free, square, 3:4, 16:9.

The capture copies to the clipboard, saves to ~/Pictures/Screenshots, and shows a floating preview for 7 seconds of idle time. Hover it for Pin, Edit, Copy, drag-out, and Close. Pin it with the pin button, Ctrl+P, T while hovered, or by dragging it. If it fades, the PNG is still saved — and the recents shelf (right edge of the next overlay) keeps your last five captures, reopenable with layers and undo history intact.

4. Annotate.

Press E or A in the capture picker to keep the editor open after the shot, or click Edit on any preview or pin. The essentials:

  • V — Select / move / resize layers (wheel scales a layer)
  • A — Arrow — press again to cycle Standard, Pointy, Curved, Double
  • T — Text (Neucha default; Shift+T cycles fonts)
  • D — Redact — press again for mosaic vs solid
  • O — OCR the whole image, text copied to clipboard
  • S — Spotlight / loupe
  • X — Cut a band out of the image (Ctrl inserts a band instead)
  • G / Shift+G — Cycle canvas growth: Framed / Overflow / Image
  • B — Cycle backdrops (gradient, window gray, off)
  • W — Switch editor between fullscreen overlay and normal window
  • Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+Shift+Z — Undo / redo
  • Enter — Copy + save and close
  • Ctrl+P / P — Pin the capture on screen and close the editor
  • Esc — Dismiss (edits are kept in the recents shelf)
  • ? — Show / hide the shortcuts card

Press ? any time — the overlay shows a readable shortcuts card in the lower left, and it stays closed across captures once you dismiss it (in the overlay; see the issues section for the windowed-editor exception).

5. The three things everyone needs to know:

  • It’s Hyprland-only, by design. Capture, layer surfaces, and window discovery use Wayland protocols plus hyprctl. Generic Wayland support is explicitly not claimed. It will not work on X11 or another compositor.
  • Screenshots save by default. Fresh captures autosave to ~/Pictures/Screenshots and copy to the clipboard. If you only want clipboard, set [output] autosave = false in the config (see below) — note this option landed in 1.22.0, so confirm it works on the -git snapshot you actually install.
  • Previews and pins are real compositor windows. They stay visible on every workspace, they appear in later screenshots if you leave them over the capture area, and closing one with the mouse currently moves your pointer (issue #206 below — use the keyboard to close a stack).

6. Config location.

No settings UI — everything is an optional INI file at ~/.config/omasnap/omasnap.conf. Every key is optional; it runs fine with no config at all.

[editor]
mode = overlay      # overlay (default) or window
window = floating   # floating (default) or tiled

[output]
autosave = true
directory = ~/Pictures/Captures
filename = screenshot-{date}_{time}-{app}

[colors]
palette = #ff375f, #ff9f0a, #ffd60a, #30d158, #0a84ff, #bf5af2, #000000, #ffffff

The filename {app} token is the Hyprland window class under the selection (e.g. firefox). Env overrides also work: OMASNAP_SCREENSHOT_DIR and OMASNAP_OCR_LANGS (e.g. eng+deu; install the matching tesseract language data first). Theme colors come from the Omarchy palette at ~/.local/state/omarchy/current/theme/colors.toml and follow live theme changes. Recents live under ~/.local/state/omasnap/recent/.

Common issues & fixes

All items below come from the project README, changelog, or the open issue tracker — none are invented. Anything not yet confirmed on Omarchy is marked as such.

Running omasnap outside a Wayland session (TTY, SSH without a display, X11) crashes with SIGABRT / exit 134

Known upstream (issue #203, fixed by PR #208, open at draft time): Qt fell back from the wayland platform plugin to xcb, found no X server, and aborted with a core dump. The fix checks for a Wayland display before starting Qt and exits cleanly with code 1 and a No Wayland display: WAYLAND_DISPLAY is not set message.

Fix: Until that lands in a build you have, only run omasnap inside your Hyprland session — never from a bare TTY. Unverified: whether the Oct 8 -git snapshot already contains the fix (the PR is dated Nov 3, so almost certainly not).

The capture preview is tiny / unreadable on a 4K panel at scale 2

Open feature request, no config yet (issue #212, Nov 5, 2026): the preview is a fixed 200 logical px wide, which the reporter calls “hard to read comfortably” on a 3840×2160 panel at scale 2. The proposed fix is a [preview] width = 250 (or scale) key in omasnap.conf.

Fix: Workaround until then: pin the preview (Ctrl+P or T while hovered) so it stays put, or open the editor (E on the preview) for a full-size view. Unverified on Omarchy: the workaround is inferred from the README, not tested.

In the windowed editor, the hotkey guide above the toolbar can’t be hidden

Open bug (issue #211, Nov 5, 2026): in the overlay editor, ? closes the shortcuts card and it stays closed; in the windowed editor (--editor window or [editor] mode = window), ? does nothing and the guide is always drawn, eating vertical space.

Fix: Workaround: use the default overlay editor, where ? works. Unverified: whether the -git snapshot behaves the same way (the report is against 1.25.0).

On two monitors, clicking Edit on a saved-capture notification opens the editor on the wrong monitor

Partially fixed upstream, still open for the notification case (PR #207, Nov 2, 2026): the toast’s Edit runs omasnap --recent with no monitor handoff, so the editor falls back to Qt’s “primary” screen — usually the laptop’s built-in panel. The 1.24.0 changelog already fixed this for preview/pin Edit (“opens the editor on the monitor showing that preview”); the open PR extends the same focused-monitor lookup to notification clicks and --file/--clipboard opens.

Fix: Workaround: open the editor from the preview or pin instead of the notification, or run omasnap --file ~/Pictures/Screenshots/<name>.png from the monitor you want. Unverified on Omarchy: multi-monitor behavior of the -git snapshot.

Clicking X on a pin throws the pointer to the center of the next pin, so you can’t click through a stack

Open bug with a fix in review (PR #206, Nov 2, 2026): closing a hovered pin hands focus to the next pin via hl.dsp.focus, and Hyprland’s focus action always warps the cursor. Keyboard closes (X, Esc, Super+W) keep the focus handoff (that’s what makes repeated X presses work); the PR makes the close button and middle-click skip it, so the next pin slides into place under your pointer.

Fix: Workaround until it lands: close pins with the keyboard — focus the pin, press X repeatedly — instead of clicking each X. Unverified on Omarchy: the PR was tested live on Hyprland 0.56.2 by its author, not on Omarchy.

Pairs well with / If you hate this, try

Pairs well with

  • grim + slurp (scripted captures piped into omasnap --clipboard for annotation — omasnap opens any clipboard image straight in the editor), wl-copy / wl-paste (omasnap’s clipboard path already uses them, so clipboard history managers keep working), and the Omarchy screen-recording flow (--notify announcements are deliberately worded like Omarchy’s saved-recording notifications).

If you hate this, try

  • grim + slurp (see below — the minimal pipeline, no editor at all), Satty (the focused Wayland annotation tool omasnap’s README cites as an inspiration — capture with grim, annotate in Satty, lighter than omasnap’s full overlay), or Flameshot (the classic selection-first annotator — but it’s an X11-era tool that needs portal setup on Hyprland and is not in the Omarchy store).

Verdict: If you want omasnap — and on Omarchy you probably do, it’s built for Hyprland — pick stable omasnap unless the -git store snapshot is newer than the stable package’s update date. grim + slurp is the right pick only when you want screenshots with zero UI; Flameshot only if you’re already fluent in it from another system and don’t mind the portal setup.

Free alternative to Shottr / CleanShot-style screenshot tools

Free alternative to Shottr / CleanShot-style screenshot tools. omasnap is free and open source, and its workflow — region capture, OCR, polished backdrops, scrolling capture — is directly inspired by Shottr (the README names it first among its inspirations). What you give up: Shottr and CleanShot are macOS apps, so this isn’t a switch from them unless you’re already moving to Linux — and omasnap has no cloud upload / share-link service (Flameshot’s Imgur upload has no equivalent here). What you keep: the fast region/window capture, one-click OCR, annotation, and the pretty framed backdrops — free forever, native on Wayland, no account, no subscription.

Frequently asked questions

Does omasnap-git work on Omarchy?

Yes — it’s built for Omarchy and Hyprland specifically (Wayland + Hyprland is the only supported target). Install with omarchy pkg add omasnap-git. Note the -git build tracks the main branch, so it can be newer or older than the stable omasnap package depending on when each was last rebuilt — check the store page’s “Updated” date.

Is omasnap-git free?

Yes. MIT + OFL-1.1 licensed open source. No paid tier, no account, no telemetry mentioned.

What’s the difference between omasnap and omasnap-git?

Same app, different build: omasnap is a tagged release (1.25.0 at draft time), omasnap-git is built from the main branch. The -git build gets unreleased features and fixes first — and unreleased bugs first. At draft time the store’s -git snapshot (2026-10-08) actually predates the stable 1.25.0 release, so check dates before choosing.

How do I take a scrolling screenshot of a long page?

omasnap --scroll, drag the region, then pick Scroll ↓/→ (you scroll the page yourself while it captures each step) or Auto ↓/→ (it scrolls for you). Frames are aligned and stitched into one image. Or press S in the capture picker before drawing.

Where do screenshots go?

~/Pictures/Screenshots by default, named screenshot-{date}_{time}-{app}.png — and they’re copied to the clipboard at the same time. Change the folder or filename pattern in ~/.config/omasnap/omasnap.conf, or set OMASNAP_SCREENSHOT_DIR. Set [output] autosave = false for clipboard-only captures.
